target_model: Probability that a borrower is 90+ days delinquent within two years (Give Me Some Credit)

event.meaning: serious delinquency: 90 or more days past due within two years

prediction.units: probability of serious delinquency within two years
prediction.r_predict: predict(model, newdata = newdata, type = "response", na.action = na.pass)

preprocessing.description: Remove the two columns with missing values
Encode the response as a factor with levels 0, 1
Standardise every predictor with the training mean and standard deviation

split.method: none: the model is fit and evaluated on the full training file

assessment.business_use: Ranking credit applicants by risk of serious delinquency
assessment.intended_population: Consumer credit borrowers scored for credit decisions
assessment.sample_population: The Give Me Some Credit training file; the code does not state its period or channel

baseline_comparison.rationale: Ranking applicants needs discrimination beyond the portfolio's delinquency rate

calibration.rationale: Predicted probabilities feed credit decisions, so they must match observed delinquency

subgroup_performance.rationale: Risk ranking should hold across borrower age bands and utilisation

stability.rationale: The model is fit on one file, so refits show how much the estimates move

sensitivity.rationale: Credit policy needs to know how the score responds to utilisation and debt

assumptions.rationale: A logit on correlated delinquency counts can separate or be collinear

substitutions.original: predictions on cs-test.csv, scaled with its own statistics
substitutions.proposed: evaluate on the training file only
substitutions.rationale: cs-test.csv has no response and is not an uploaded dataset

baseline_r:
cs_training = read.csv("inputs/cs-training.csv")
cs_training = cs_training[,(-1)]
cs_training$MonthlyIncome <- NULL
cs_training$NumberOfDependents <- NULL
cs_training$SeriousDlqin2yrs = factor(cs_training$SeriousDlqin2yrs, levels = c(0,1))
cs_training[-1] = scale(cs_training[-1])
RegModel = glm(formula = cs_training$SeriousDlqin2yrs ~ .,
               family = binomial,
               data = cs_training)
